text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- The future distribution of funds to the less developed countries of the European Union will be based on unemployment rates and national wealth which may cause Lisbon and the Tagus valley to loose out.
- According to European Commissioner for Agriculture, Frans Fischler, the Common Agriculture Policy (CAP) is good for Portugal since local agriculture is better now than 10 years ago.
- The government must give financial aid to state cereal company EPAC, which has 50 billion escudos of liabilities, if the company is to be privatised second half of 1997 or beginning of 1998.
- Banking groups Caixa Geral de Depositos and Banco Portugues de Investimentos lead rankings in buying intentions for shares in state electricity company EDP.
- Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro Valls said the Pope accepted an invitation to visit Fatima this year. No date set.

- The European Commission's unit for Coordination of the Fight Against Fraud is investigating parallel imports of olive oil in 1993 and 1994 since it may have caused a rise in the production and export numbers of Portugal, Italy and Spain and and an undue increase in community subsidies.
